counter_review: Removing reports must not remove mode synchronization or page-domain operations.
Segment indices 0..5 match CCPU use; moving declarations alone is not an algorithm simplification.
Original i386/dpmi386.c reads offsets 0,2,6,8,12. CCPU setters execute descriptor loads rather than passive context writes.
pm_entry_contract_fixture invalid-IDT case counts register writes but does not check gdt; its pass cannot prove unchanged state.
c_xtrn.c catches CPU exceptions and returns interface_error; passive original CONTEXT stores do not share that failure contract. Mock setters cannot prove delivery.
Provider returns 1 when inactive and otherwise fails only if PE=0. This path has set PE; paging/GDT restoration is not redundant.
No transition or return value depends on the report.
Original dpmi386.c uses offsets 0,2,4,6,8; load_data_seg/load_stack_seg update base/selector in real mode but leave attribute cache, so pseudo refresh is not duplicate setter work.
Keep the preceding guest continuation loads.
c_setCS calls load_code_seg and validates protected selectors when PE=1; original DOSX real CS is not guaranteed a valid protected selector.
load_pseudo_descr changes limit, R/W/E/C/X/DPL, not base. It is necessary for some transitions but reset/IRET usage alone does not prove this helper requires all six resets.
Keep cache refresh pending its own semantic review.
Provider updates RM_BIT through SAS only after fast selector allocation; original dpmi386.c publishes same mode bit for guest gate.
int21map callers restore state later; source c_setCS/SS validates now and returns interface_error. Comment rationale is not proof every call needs both carriers.
Failure return cannot be inferred merely from discarded status; provider has no other false return.
Do not remove page-domain restore with report.
